global_read: global.json (12:18) shows a sharp risk-on reversal in the oil/conflict tape overnight: Brent $90.50 (-6.49% 1d) as the US and Iran both paused strikes for a second straight night, easing the acute Middle East supply-shock fear that had pushed Brent back above $100 on Saturday after Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's Jizan and Yanbu refining/export complexes directly (the first such attack on Saudi oil infrastructure since 2022). VIX at 18.58 is still elevated (+12.38% 1d, reflecting Friday's spike into that Houthi attack) and gold is firm ($4098.9, +0.77% 1d) -- so the fear gauge and safe-haven bid have not yet caught up to today's oil relief. PKR (277.74) and DXY (101.2) are both steady, i.e. no FX stress from the whipsaw either way. Net: today's global tape is genuinely more constructive than Friday's, but it is a fragile, unannounced pause (not a signed deal) sitting on top of a larger unresolved escalation (Houthis now directly hitting Saudi refining capacity) -- a relief rally, not a resolved risk.
drivers: US and Iran both paused strikes for a second straight night (into 2026-07-26); an Iranian official said Tehran will keep holding fire 'as long as the US maintains its pause' -- an unannounced, informal truce, not a signed ceasefire, with talks continuing via Oman on the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.npr.org/2026/07/26/g-s1-135593/us-pauses-attacks-iran-second-day-tehran, https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/26/us-and-iran-hit-pause-on-strikes-for-second-day, https://boereport.com/2026/07/26/iran-will-halt-attacks-as-long-as-us-maintains-pause-iranian-source-says-after-trump-calls-off-strikes/)

Even as the US-Iran front paused, the war spread to a new and arguably bigger energy-security front: Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's Jizan and Yanbu refining/export complexes directly on 2026-07-25 (first direct hit on Saudi oil infrastructure since 2022), briefly pushing Brent back above $100 before today's pullback -- Jizan alone processes ~400,000 bpd (~4% of Aramco's output); a Patriot battery intercepted missiles aimed at Yanbu (https://www.hngn.com/articles/272350/20260725/houthi-rebels-strike-saudi-aramco-refineries-jizan-yanbu-oil-prices-surge-past-100.htm, https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2026/07/25/houthis-attack-saudi-aramco-sites-with-yemen-at-risk-of-renewed-war/)

KSE-100 opened the new week sharply higher on the pause news plus MPC-hold optimism: PSX's own market-summary showed the index up as much as +5,263.79 points (+2.99%) intraday to 176,284.99 (prior confirmed close 171,021.20, Fri 2026-07-24), corroborated by Pakistan Observer/PakTribune at +5,151pts/+3.01% to 176,172.20 -- the desk's own escalation.json trigger for this run (https://pakobserver.net/psx-climbs-over-5000-points-on-easing-middle-east-situation-policy-rate-optimism/, state/escalation.json)

SBP's 2026-07-27 MPC decision (first meeting of FY27) had NOT been announced as of this 11:00-12:25 PKT checkpoint. A Topline Securities poll (97% hold / 3% cut) and a separate Business Recorder analyst poll both point to a hold at 11.5%; SBP's own monetary-policy page still shows the last announced decision as 2026-06-15 (hold, 4th FY26 MPC), confirming no 07-27 print has posted yet (https://www.brecorder.com/news/amp/40431259, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620304/economists-urge-sbp-to-hold-rate-at-115, https://www.sbp.org.pk/m_policy/mon.asp)

Desk geo-risk radar (state/georisk.json, updated 12:18) reads 65/100 'elevated', up from Friday's 61 'moderate' composite even after today's oil pullback -- conflict/escalation stress is pinned at 100 and energy-shock stress at 78, both reflecting the weekend's Houthi-on-Aramco escalation; per desk rules an elevated geo-risk band argues against a risk-on call even where domestic anchors (SBP hold expectation, easing CPI, S&P upgrade) are holding up (state/georisk.json)

Carried forward, unchanged this run (re-checked, no update found): CPI eased to 11.1% YoY in June 2026 (from 11.7% in May), first oil-shock-affected print due 2026-08-01 (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40428129/june-cpi-inflation-up-111pc-yoy); S&P Global upgraded Pakistan's sovereign rating to 'B' from 'B-' on 2026-07-22 (https://www.dawn.com/news/2017530); SBP reserves at $17.26bn as of 2026-07-17 (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619918/sbp-reserves-rise-33m-to-1726b)

Net regime read: today's evidence is genuinely mixed and better than Friday's, so the desk moves off risk-off, but the underlying escalation is not resolved -- it merely rotated fronts (Iran-US pause vs. a fresh, direct Houthi strike on Saudi refining capacity), the SBP decision is still an open event risk into the close, and the geo-risk composite itself ticked up to 'elevated'. That combination -- real relief in the price tape and in oil, against an unresolved and arguably escalated multi-front energy conflict plus a pending policy decision -- argues for neutral, not risk-on: respect the rally in existing favored names, but do not chase it as a green light for broad new risk.

favored: E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI -- still net beneficiaries of an oil tape that, even after today's pullback, remains +23.7% over 1 month and structurally elevated by the Hormuz/Bab-el-Mandeb/Aramco chokepoint stack)
banks (T-bill yields still above the 11.5% policy rate into today's MPC outcome, and the S&P sovereign upgrade is a direct credit-quality tailwind; an SBP hold removes a source of uncertainty)
fertilizer (domestic-demand defensive, low direct oil-import beta)
avoid: OMCs (current account back in monthly deficit; a whipsawing $90-100+ oil tape compounds margin-timing/circular-debt risk on fuel-price pass-through)
cement (energy-cost sensitive; input-cost pressure evident even before this latest oil leg)
textiles/exporters (current account swung back to deficit in June; Red Sea/Bab-el-Mandeb and now direct Saudi-refinery-strike freight/insurance risk is live via the Houthi attacks)
